Course Structure








Session
When
Format




Core sessions
Tuesday and Thursday, 1.5 hours each
Interactive teaching, conceptual discussions and problem-solving


Learning clinic (optional)
Friday, 1 hour
Reflections, spill-over topics, and student-led activity discussions



Duration: three weeks.

title: About the Course
text:
Learning Activities

Homework and small programming-based projects are introduced at appropriate points during the course.
Activities can be completed individually or in groups.
Learners are encouraged to use programming tools, AI agents and LLMs to explore concepts, solve problems, test ideas and develop solutions.
Groups or individuals can showcase their work during the weekly optional session or the final week.







Note



Activities are intended for learning and exploration, not assessment. There are no graded assignments, quizzes, end-of-course examinations or completion certificates.

title: About the Course
text:
Why Take This Course?







What it means for you
Benefit




Revisit and strengthen mechanics fundamentals before pursuing postgraduate education or specialising in a technical area.
Foundations for further learning


Apply mechanics to projects at work or personal projects, and explore opportunities to combine your existing technical expertise with new domains.
Expand your technical capabilities


Discuss problems, challenge assumptions, learn from peers and explore multiple approaches rather than simply following worked examples.
Learn through interaction and collaboration


Learn to frame engineering problems, use AI agents and LLMs to explore solutions, write and execute code, and critically evaluate the results. AI can assist with the work, but engineering understanding is essential to judge whether the answers make sense.
Become an effective AI-enabled engineer



Because nothing is graded, your time goes into understanding and building rather than into preparing for tests, so the hours you invest go directly into skills you can reuse.

title: About the Course
text:
Learning Philosophy






Tip



The emphasis is on understanding, exploration and application rather than examinations, grades or certificates. The objective is not just to learn mechanics, but to develop the confidence to use it as an engineering tool in an increasingly AI-enabled workplace.
